subtopic: Caring for a sick parent while studying
subtype: Approach: talk to teachers about accommodations [Action]
passage:
I'll tell you what worked for me, beta. When I was twenty-one, my mother had a long illness, and I was drowning in missed lectures. I'm Santosh. I was scared to speak to anyone at the department, because I didn't want to look like someone making excuses.

But one Monday I knocked on Professor Sabina's door. She was the head. I told her plainly what was happening at home, said I'd miss some classes, and asked two things: a little flexibility on deadlines, and a way to get the class notes online.

She listened, then said, "Why didn't you come sooner?" She gave me two extra weeks on one paper and arranged for a classmate to share the notes. It cost me an awkward ten minutes. Not asking would have cost much more.

qa.q: Whose door did Santosh knock on that Monday?
Why was Santosh reluctant to speak to anyone at the department?
qa.a: Santosh was afraid of looking like someone making excuses, so pride and embarrassment held the request back.

qa.q: What turning point in the story changed Santosh's semester, and what could have happened otherwise?
qa.a: Knocking on the door and asking plainly changed things; without it, missed lectures and deadlines would probably have piled up unnoticed.

qa.q: How does Professor Sabina see the request when Santosh finally comes?
qa.a: Professor Sabina listens without judgement, and asking why Santosh did not come sooner suggests she would gladly have helped earlier.

grounding: The student explains the situation to the department head and asks for deadline flexibility and class notes online.

Santosh had two days before the lab report deadline and a hospital appointment for his mother at the same hour as Thursday's practical. The department office closed at four. It was three twenty.
He ran across the campus and knocked on Professor Hafsa's door, out of breath. "Ma'am, I need five minutes."
She waved him in. He explained quickly: his mother's treatment, the appointments clashing with practicals, the lab report he couldn't finish in time.
"What are you asking for?" she said.
"An extension of a week on the report. And if the Thursday practical could be recorded, or I could get notes."
Professor Hafsa opened a file on her screen. "We have a form for exactly this. Fill it today, attach the appointment letter. I'll approve the extension. For practicals, I'll ask the lab assistant to share notes and you can do a make-up session."
Santosh filled the form at 3:50, ten minutes before closing.

qa.q: What time did the department office close?
How was Santosh feeling when he reached the door?
qa.a: He was anxious and rushed, arriving out of breath with the office about to close.

qa.q: What else could Santosh do to avoid a last-minute rush next time?
qa.a: He could tell the department as soon as new appointments are scheduled, since there is a set process when asked early.

qa.q: How does the request look from Professor Hafsa's side?
qa.a: Professor Hafsa sees a clear, reasonable request and already has a form and options ready, so helping is straightforward.

grounding: Shows the student explaining a parent's illness to the department head and asking for deadline flexibility and access to class material.

subtopic: Caring for a sick parent while studying

passage:
Chandrika took the auto from her Hyderabad colony to college on Monday with an appointment letter in her bag and a list on her phone. Her father's treatment meant she'd miss most afternoon classes for the next two months.
Her friend Charu had said, "Just email everyone at the end if you fall behind." Chandrika wanted to ask before that happened.
She went to the head of department's office first thing. She showed the letter and explained: afternoons at the hospital, three assignments due in that time, and a mid-semester exam she could still take.
"What would help?" the head asked.
"Flexibility on the assignment dates, and access to the recorded lectures or notes for afternoon classes."
The head called the course coordinator on speakerphone. By noon Chandrika had an email: new due dates for two assignments, and a shared folder where teachers would upload notes.
She forwarded it to Charu with one line: "Asked early. Worked."

qa.q: What did Chandrika show the head of department?
Why did Chandrika want to ask before falling behind, and how did she feel afterwards?
qa.a: She was worried that waiting would make it harder, and afterwards she felt relieved and a little proud, texting 'Asked early. Worked.'

qa.q: What else could Chandrika ask for if treatment runs longer than two months?
qa.a: She could go back early and ask to extend the arrangement, since the department has already shown it can adjust.

qa.q: How might Charu see Chandrika's approach after the message?
qa.a: Charu may realise her own advice to wait was risky, and feel glad that asking early paid off for her friend.

grounding: Shows the student telling the department head about a parent's illness early and getting deadline flexibility and access to class notes.
